subject: Next steps: Pilot & SDK compatibility checklist for Skylark Health
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@skylarkhealth.com>, Pat Lee <pat.lee@skylarkhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:20:00Z
Subject: Next steps: Pilot & SDK compatibility checklist for Skylark Health

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed pilot plan so we all have the same view.

Summary of the pain points you described:
- High inference cost and opaque token billing across multiple model variants.
- Latency spikes for multi-user workflows (peak 95th percentile latency > 250ms).
- Need for HIPAA-safe handling of PHI and customer-managed keys.
- Tight timeline for a Q1 product launch that requires predictable SLA and a repeatable onboarding path.

Current stack (from call): Kubernetes + in-house model server, OAuth2 for auth, models trained in PyTorch and exported to ONNX.

Success criteria for the pilot (mutually agreed):
1) 95th percentile latency for defined workload < 120ms for generation requests at 500 concurrent connections.
2) Clear cost baseline: reduce per-1k-token cost by at least 25% vs current fleet using batching/cache.
3) Security: VPC deployment option + KMS integration for key management and audit logs available to Skylark.
4) API/SDK compatibility: ability to call Redwood APIs from Python and Go with minimal adapter work.

Proposed pilot timeline & milestones (6-week pilot):
- Week 0 (pre-work): NDA/POC SOW signoff, access & account setup.
- Week 1: Private sandbox provisioned (VPC), API keys, baseline latency/cost profiling.
- Week 2: Model onboarding & SDK integration (Python + Go clients).
- Week 3: Traffic shaping & scale test (continuous batching enabled).
- Week 4: Cost optimization (quantization recommendations, cache rules).
- Week 5: Security review & logging/audit verification.
- Week 6: Joint validation, success metric review, go/no-go recommendation.

Ownership (proposed):
- Skylark: Alex Morgan (product owner), Pat Lee (engineering lead)
- Redwood: Rachel Kim (sales lead, overall), Ben Carter (SE lead for integration), Neha Kapoor (solutions & security contact)

Attachments I am sending with this email: redwood_pilot_plan_v1.pdf (pilot plan / milestones), security_matrix_skylark.xlsx (high-level controls mapping).

Immediate next steps:
- Can you confirm the pilot start week (we proposed week of Oct 12)?
- Please confirm Alex/Pat as owners and whether your infra team can provision a test namespace with access to OAuth2 tokens for our SE to test.
- Ben/Neha: please review the security matrix and be ready to run through it with Skylark next call.

Thanks — I’ll send a calendar invite once Alex confirms a start date.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Rachel — this captures our discussion well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot start: Oct 12 week works for us (we can kick off with an internal sync on Oct 13).
- Auth: we use OAuth2 + internal SSO (Okta). We will need Redwood to support SSO for the private deployment and a KMS integration for key rotation.
- Stack detail: our serving layer is a custom Kubernetes + Knative setup; most of our engineers prefer Go clients but we have Python data scientists who will experiment with the Python SDK.
- Data handling: any PHI must remain in our VPC; happy to walk through the security matrix in detail.

One ask: can you confirm whether Redwood's Go SDK supports streaming responses and function/tool calls (we rely on streaming for progressive UI updates)? Also, do you have a short example of Go usage with example auth header?

Attached: I reviewed the pilot plan and it looks good — I’ll ask Pat to set up an internal namespace and grant Ben access next week.

Alex
Product Manager, Skylark Health
